#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Archive the contents of /etc and /home into a compressed tarball.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/archive_etc_home.sh [output-directory]
#
# Default output directory: ./archives
#
# Notes:
# - Run with sudo/root if you need to include files that are not readable by
#   the current user.
# - The archive stores paths relative to /, e.g. etc/hosts and home/user/file.

OUTPUT_DIR="${1:-./archives}"
TIMESTAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
HOSTNAME_SAFE="$(hostname | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')"
ARCHIVE_NAME="etc-home-${HOSTNAME_SAFE}-${TIMESTAMP}.tar.gz"
ARCHIVE_PATH="${OUTPUT_DIR%/}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}"

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

echo "Creating archive: $ARCHIVE_PATH"

tar \
  --create \
  --gzip \
  --file "$ARCHIVE_PATH" \
  --directory / \
  --warning=no-file-changed \
  etc home

echo "Archive created successfully: $ARCHIVE_PATH"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Create SSH tunnels for secure data transfer.
#
# Modes:
#   local  - Forward a local port to a host/port reachable from the SSH server.
#   socks  - Create a local SOCKS proxy over SSH.
#
# Examples:
#   # Forward local port 1873 to remote server's rsync daemon on 127.0.0.1:873
#   ./scripts/ssh_tunnel.sh local 1873 127.0.0.1 873 backup-user backup.example.com
#
#   # Same, with custom SSH port and key
#   ./scripts/ssh_tunnel.sh local 1873 127.0.0.1 873 backup-user backup.example.com 2222 ~/.ssh/backup_key
#
#   # Create a SOCKS proxy on localhost:1080 through the remote server
#   ./scripts/ssh_tunnel.sh socks 1080 backup-user backup.example.com
#
#   # Transfer through local tunnel, for example with rsync daemon:
#   rsync -av ./data/ rsync://127.0.0.1:1873/module/
#
# Notes:
# - This binds only to 127.0.0.1 by default, so the tunnel is not exposed on the LAN.
# - The command runs in the foreground. Keep the terminal open while transferring.
# - Press Ctrl+C to close the tunnel.

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
Usage:
  ssh_tunnel.sh local <local_port> <target_host> <target_port> <ssh_user> <ssh_host> [ssh_port] [identity_file]
  ssh_tunnel.sh socks <local_port> <ssh_user> <ssh_host> [ssh_port] [identity_file]

Examples:
  ssh_tunnel.sh local 1873 127.0.0.1 873 backup-user backup.example.com
  ssh_tunnel.sh local 1873 127.0.0.1 873 backup-user backup.example.com 2222 ~/.ssh/backup_key
  ssh_tunnel.sh socks 1080 backup-user backup.example.com
USAGE
}

require_port() {
  local value="$1"
  local name="$2"
  if ! [[ "$value" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( value < 1 || value > 65535 )); then
    echo "Error: $name must be a TCP port number from 1 to 65535." >&2
    exit 2
  fi
}

if [[ $# -lt 1 ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 2
fi

MODE="$1"
shift

SSH_OPTS=(
  -N
  -T
  -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes
  -o ServerAliveInterval=60
  -o ServerAliveCountMax=3
)

case "$MODE" in
  local)
    if [[ $# -lt 5 || $# -gt 7 ]]; then
      usage >&2
      exit 2
    fi

    LOCAL_PORT="$1"
    TARGET_HOST="$2"
    TARGET_PORT="$3"
    SSH_USER="$4"
    SSH_HOST="$5"
    SSH_PORT="${6:-22}"
    IDENTITY_FILE="${7:-}"

    require_port "$LOCAL_PORT" "local_port"
    require_port "$TARGET_PORT" "target_port"
    require_port "$SSH_PORT" "ssh_port"

    if [[ -n "$IDENTITY_FILE" ]]; then
      SSH_OPTS+=(-i "$IDENTITY_FILE")
    fi

    echo "Opening local SSH tunnel: 127.0.0.1:${LOCAL_PORT} -> ${TARGET_HOST}:${TARGET_PORT} via ${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}:${SSH_PORT}"
    exec ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" \
      -p "$SSH_PORT" \
      -L "127.0.0.1:${LOCAL_PORT}:${TARGET_HOST}:${TARGET_PORT}" \
      "${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}"
    ;;

  socks)
    if [[ $# -lt 3 || $# -gt 5 ]]; then
      usage >&2
      exit 2
    fi

    LOCAL_PORT="$1"
    SSH_USER="$2"
    SSH_HOST="$3"
    SSH_PORT="${4:-22}"
    IDENTITY_FILE="${5:-}"

    require_port "$LOCAL_PORT" "local_port"
    require_port "$SSH_PORT" "ssh_port"

    if [[ -n "$IDENTITY_FILE" ]]; then
      SSH_OPTS+=(-i "$IDENTITY_FILE")
    fi

    echo "Opening SOCKS SSH tunnel: socks5://127.0.0.1:${LOCAL_PORT} via ${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}:${SSH_PORT}"
    exec ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" \
      -p "$SSH_PORT" \
      -D "127.0.0.1:${LOCAL_PORT}" \
      "${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}"
    ;;

  -h|--help|help)
    usage
    ;;

  *)
    echo "Error: unknown mode: $MODE" >&2
    usage >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Install and enable the systemd timer that runs archive_etc_home.sh daily.
#
# Usage:
#   sudo ./scripts/install_archive_timer.sh

if [[ "${EUID}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  echo "Error: run as root, for example: sudo $0" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Error: systemctl was not found. This system does not appear to use systemd." >&2
  exit 1
fi

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORKSPACE_DIR="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
UNIT_SRC_DIR="${WORKSPACE_DIR}/systemd"
UNIT_DST_DIR="/etc/systemd/system"
BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups/openclaw-archives"

install -d -m 0755 "$BACKUP_DIR"
install -m 0644 "${UNIT_SRC_DIR}/archive-etc-home.service" "${UNIT_DST_DIR}/archive-etc-home.service"
install -m 0644 "${UNIT_SRC_DIR}/archive-etc-home.timer" "${UNIT_DST_DIR}/archive-etc-home.timer"

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now archive-etc-home.timer

echo "Installed and enabled archive-etc-home.timer"
echo "Next scheduled run:"
systemctl list-timers archive-etc-home.timer --no-pager

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Verify that a local archive was successfully transferred to remote storage.
#
# This compares file size and SHA-256 checksum between a local archive and a
# remote copy accessible over SSH.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/verify_archive_transfer.sh <local_archive|local_dir> <ssh_user> <ssh_host> <remote_path_or_dir> [ssh_port] [identity_file]
#
# Examples:
#   # Verify a specific archive against a specific remote file
#   ./scripts/verify_archive_transfer.sh ./archives/etc-home-host-20260520T100000Z.tar.gz backup backup.example.com /srv/backups/etc-home-host-20260520T100000Z.tar.gz
#
#   # Verify the newest *.tar.gz in a local directory against a remote directory
#   ./scripts/verify_archive_transfer.sh ./archives backup backup.example.com /srv/backups
#
#   # Custom SSH port and identity key
#   ./scripts/verify_archive_transfer.sh ./archives backup backup.example.com /srv/backups 2222 ~/.ssh/backup_key

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
Usage:
  verify_archive_transfer.sh <local_archive|local_dir> <ssh_user> <ssh_host> <remote_path_or_dir> [ssh_port] [identity_file]

Examples:
  verify_archive_transfer.sh ./archives backup backup.example.com /srv/backups
  verify_archive_transfer.sh ./archives/file.tar.gz backup backup.example.com /srv/backups/file.tar.gz
  verify_archive_transfer.sh ./archives backup backup.example.com /srv/backups 2222 ~/.ssh/backup_key
USAGE
}

require_port() {
  local value="$1"
  if ! [[ "$value" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( value < 1 || value > 65535 )); then
    echo "Error: ssh_port must be a TCP port number from 1 to 65535." >&2
    exit 2
  fi
}

quote_remote_arg() {
  printf '%q' "$1"
}

if [[ $# -lt 4 || $# -gt 6 ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 2
fi

LOCAL_INPUT="$1"
SSH_USER="$2"
SSH_HOST="$3"
REMOTE_INPUT="$4"
SSH_PORT="${5:-22}"
IDENTITY_FILE="${6:-}"

require_port "$SSH_PORT"

SSH_OPTS=(
  -p "$SSH_PORT"
  -o BatchMode=yes
  -o ConnectTimeout=15
  -o ServerAliveInterval=30
  -o ServerAliveCountMax=2
)

if [[ -n "$IDENTITY_FILE" ]]; then
  SSH_OPTS+=(-i "$IDENTITY_FILE")
fi

if [[ -d "$LOCAL_INPUT" ]]; then
  LOCAL_FILE="$(find "$LOCAL_INPUT" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -nr | awk 'NR==1 {sub(/^[^ ]+ /, ""); print}')"
  if [[ -z "${LOCAL_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    echo "Error: no *.tar.gz archives found in local directory: $LOCAL_INPUT" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
else
  LOCAL_FILE="$LOCAL_INPUT"
fi

if [[ ! -f "$LOCAL_FILE" ]]; then
  echo "Error: local archive not found: $LOCAL_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

LOCAL_BASENAME="$(basename -- "$LOCAL_FILE")"

# If the remote input ends with /, treat it as a directory. Otherwise, first
# ask the remote side whether it is a directory; if that check fails, treat it
# as a file path.
if [[ "$REMOTE_INPUT" == */ ]]; then
  REMOTE_FILE="${REMOTE_INPUT%/}/${LOCAL_BASENAME}"
else
  REMOTE_QUOTED="$(quote_remote_arg "$REMOTE_INPUT")"
  if ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}" "test -d ${REMOTE_QUOTED}" 2>/dev/null; then
    REMOTE_FILE="${REMOTE_INPUT%/}/${LOCAL_BASENAME}"
  else
    REMOTE_FILE="$REMOTE_INPUT"
  fi
fi

LOCAL_SIZE="$(stat -c '%s' "$LOCAL_FILE")"
LOCAL_SHA256="$(sha256sum "$LOCAL_FILE" | awk '{print $1}')"
REMOTE_FILE_QUOTED="$(quote_remote_arg "$REMOTE_FILE")"

read -r REMOTE_SIZE REMOTE_SHA256 < <(
  ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}" \
    "test -f ${REMOTE_FILE_QUOTED} && stat -c '%s' ${REMOTE_FILE_QUOTED} && sha256sum ${REMOTE_FILE_QUOTED} | awk '{print \$1}'" \
    | awk 'NR==1 {size=$1} NR==2 {sha=$1} END {if (size && sha) print size, sha}'
)

if [[ -z "${REMOTE_SIZE:-}" || -z "${REMOTE_SHA256:-}" ]]; then
  echo "Verification failed: remote archive not found or could not be read: ${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}:${REMOTE_FILE}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Local file:  $LOCAL_FILE"
echo "Remote file: ${SSH_USER}@${SSH_HOST}:${REMOTE_FILE}"
echo "Local size:  $LOCAL_SIZE"
echo "Remote size: $REMOTE_SIZE"
echo "Local SHA:   $LOCAL_SHA256"
echo "Remote SHA:  $REMOTE_SHA256"

if [[ "$LOCAL_SIZE" == "$REMOTE_SIZE" && "$LOCAL_SHA256" == "$REMOTE_SHA256" ]]; then
  echo "Verification successful: remote archive matches local archive."
  exit 0
fi

echo "Verification failed: remote archive differs from local archive." >&2
exit 1
